From √naphash (breathe); the breathing-throat / life-force / animate-self. 755 occurrences. The most-frequent abstract-noun in OT. Considered: soul, life, self, person, breath, throat, desire. The Hebrew kernel is the breathing-living-creature (Gen 2:7 'man became a living nephesh'); the same word covers human (Gen 2:7), animal (Gen 1:20-24; 9:10-16), corpse (Lev 21:1; Num 6:6 — 'dead nephesh'), the seat-of-desire (Deu 12:15; 14:26), and the personal-pronoun-substitute (Num 19:13). KJV uniformly 'soul'; ESV/NIV split 'soul/life/person'. Concordant 'soul' is preserved across all 755 occurrences with the toelichting noting that Hebrew nephesh is not the immortal-soul of Greek-philosophy: nephesh dies (Eze 18:4 'the soul that sins shall die') and nephesh is identified with blood (Gen 9:4-5; Lev 17:11). The breathing-throat / life-force kernel is preserved through the single rendering.

Verb of lifting / carrying / bearing / forgiving / taking. 651 occurrences — among highest-frequency verbs in OT. The kernel is upward-motion (the etymology) extended to: bear-burden (Num 11:14), bear-sin (Lev 16:22), forgive (lift-away sin, Ex 34:7), take-wife (Ru 1:4; 4:13), receive (Ezr 9:7), exalt (Ps 24:7), endure (Lam 3:27), respect-persons (lit. 'lift-face', Lev 19:15). KJV uses 'bear / take / lift / forgive' contextually. Concordant 'lift' is the kernel; the bear/forgive/take/respect renderings are downstream extensions visible in render-context. Distinguished from H5414 nathan ('give'), H6213 asah ('do/make'), H3947 laqach ('take').

Reed-grass especially of the Reed-Sea (yam-suph) (Ex 2:3,5; 10:19; 13:18; 15:4,22; 23:31; Num 14:25; 21:4,14; 33:10,11; Deu 1:1,40; 2:1; 11:4; Jos 2:10; 4:23; 24:6; Jdg 11:16; 1Ki 9:26; Neh 9:9; Job 38:11 (variant); Ps 106:7,9,22; 136:13,15; Isa 19:6; Jer 49:21; Jon 2:6 [5]). 28 occurrences. Standard. The famous 'Sea-of-Reeds' (yam-suph) is traditionally rendered 'Red Sea' in English-Bible-tradition (KJV/ESV) following LXX 'erythra thalassa', but the Hebrew kernel is 'reed' not 'red'.
